messages.content:
You are FIXING a short WhatsApp quiz written for the children who sat in ONE real lesson. 3 of its 8 questions were rejected by our checks. You are writing ONE replacement for each. Every other question is good and is staying exactly as it is — do not touch it, do not return it.

QUIZ LANGUAGE: English. Write EVERYTHING in English — every stem, option, explanation and feedback — even though the lesson was taught in Urdu: translate the teacher's own words and keep the lesson's own examples, numbers and names. An Urdu word may appear only when quoting a term the class used, in quotation marks.

REWRITE THESE QUESTIONS: q2, q3, q5

WHAT THESE CHILDREN WERE MEANT TO LEARN. A replacement stays on its own question's SLO, at its own question's level.
- S1 [taught at understand] Identify numbers from 0 to 9.
- S2 [taught at understand] Count numbers from 0 to 9.
- S3 [taught at understand] Show numbers 0 to 9 in different forms (objects, drawings, fingers).
- S4 [taught at understand] Match numerals to their corresponding quantities shown in different forms.

THE LESSON'S OWN MATERIAL — dress the replacement in it, so a child recognises the class in the quiz.
topic as the teacher named it: Numbers All Around Us - Draw & Match to Fingers
the lesson's own examples: chalk dots on the board (seven dots); hands showing different numbers of raised fingers (open hand, two raised fingers, one raised finger); petals at the bottom of a picture; tree branches; stem leaves
the words used in class: number («numbers»), count, numeral, object («objects»), drawing («drawings»), finger («fingers»)

THE QUESTIONS THAT ARE STAYING. A replacement must not ask one of these again, and must not have the same answer as one of them.
  q0: Which of these is the numeral for seven?
  q1: How many chalk dots are there?
  q4: Which of these shows the number five?
  q6: Which is the correct way to count?
  q7: Which of these is a numeral?

EVERY QUESTION TESTS SOMETHING NO OTHER QUESTION TESTS. No two questions in the quiz may have the same correct answer on the same fact: the same question with its options in another order, with other wrong options, or with a few words added or changed is the SAME question, and a child would answer it twice. A question shape may be used again only with different numbers or a different item from the lesson (round 18, then round 16; the article before "kite", then before "tree"), so that its correct answer is different too. Before you return, read the questions side by side: where two test the same thing, write a question on something else in place of the later one, keeping the number of questions as it is.

REJECTED — write one new question for each, except a question marked REPAIR IN PLACE: return that one as it stands, with only the words its complaints name changed.

q2 · slo_id "S3" · level "understand"
  the question being thrown away: "Which hand shows two fingers?"
  its options were: P | Q | R
  why it was rejected:
    - q2: FIGURE_INDISTINCT — 3 parts are the same "hand" drawing and differ only by count, which the question never names; a child cannot tell these pictures apart: draw different things, or make them differ by something drawn that the question names (a colour, a count, a size)

q3 · slo_id "S4" · level "apply"
  the question being thrown away: "What numeral matches these petals?"
  its options were: 5 | 6 | 7
  why it was rejected:
    - q3: FIGURE_SHOWS_KEY — the picture draws exactly 5 and 5 is the answer, so the child reads the key off the picture; draw the situation (all the numbers in the options, or the groups), never only the answer

q5 · slo_id "S4" · level "understand"
  the question being thrown away: "What numeral matches these leaves?"
  its options were: 4 | 3 | 5
  why it was rejected:
    - q5: FIGURE_SHOWS_KEY — the picture draws exactly 3 and 3 is the answer, so the child reads the key off the picture; draw the situation (all the numbers in the options, or the groups), never only the answer
